iceberg: The seaward end of a glacier.
iceblink: A glare in the sky caused by reflection of light from an ice field.
iceboating: The act of travelling in a iceboat.
icebound: Completely surrounded by ice and therefore unable to move.
icebox: A box or compartment containing ice, typically used to keep provisions cool.
icebreaker: A ship designed to break through ice so that it, or other ships coming behind, can navigate on frozen seas.
icefall: A relatively rapid and turbulent flow of ice, somewhat analogous to a waterfall.
icehouse: A warehouse for the storage of ice for commercial purposes.
icekhana: A motorkhana that takes place on a frozen lake.
iceman: A person who trades in ice; a person employed to deliver block ice to those lacking electric refrigeration.
ich: Ichthyophthiriasis, a parasitic infection of freshwater fish caused by ciliates of genus Ichthyophthirius.
ichneumon: An Egyptian mongoose (Herpestes ichneumon), found in Africa and southern Europe.
ichnite: A fossilized footprint or track of an animal.
ichor: The liquid said to flow in place of blood in the veins of the gods.
ichthyic: Of, pertaining to, or like fish; piscine.
ichthyofauna: The fish of a particular region.
ichthyologist: An expert in ichthyology: one who studies fishes.
ichthyology: A branch of zoology that studies fish.
ichthyosaur: Any fishlike marine reptiles of the extinct order †Ichthyosauria of the early Triassic to the late Cretaceous period, that had a body somewhat like a porpoise.
ichthyosaurian: Of or relating to the Ichthyosauria.
icicle: A drooping, tapering shape of ice.
icier: comparative form of icy: more icy
iciest: superlative form of icy: most icy
icily: In the manner of ice; with a cold or chilling effect.
iciness: The state or quality of being icy or very cold; frigidity.
icing: A sweet, often creamy and thick glaze made primarily of sugar, often enriched with ingredients like butter, egg whites, or flavorings, typically used for baked goods.
ickier: comparative form of icky: more icky
ickiest: superlative form of icky: most icky
ickiness: The state or condition of being icky.
icon: An image, symbol, picture, portrait, or other representation, usually as an object of religious devotion.
iconic: Relating to, or having the characteristics of, an icon.
iconical: Pertaining to or consisting of images or icons.
iconically: In a way or to an extent that is iconic
iconicity: the state of being iconic (in all meanings)
iconoclasm: The belief in, participation in, or sanction of destroying religious icons and other symbols or monuments, usually with religious or political motives.
iconoclast: One who destroys religious images or icons, especially an opponent of the Orthodox Church in the 8th and 9th centuries, or a Puritan during the European Reformation.
iconoclastic: Characterized by attack on established and accepted beliefs, customs, or institutions; of or pertaining to iconoclasm.
iconography: A set of specified or traditional symbolic forms associated with the subject or theme of a stylized genre of art.
iconolatry: The use of images as symbols that provide an inspiration and aid to worship.
iconology: The study of icons in art or art history.
iconoscope: an early television camera having a mosaic of photoactive cells
iconostasis: A wall of icons between the sanctuary and the nave in an Eastern Orthodox church.
icosahedral: Of, relating to, or having the shape of an icosahedron.
icteric: Jaundiced (having icterus); having yellowing of the skin, mucous membranes of the sclerae of the eyes, or other parts of the body.
icterus: An excess of bile pigments in the blood; jaundice.
ictic: Pertaining to, or caused by, a blow; sudden; abrupt.
icy: Pertaining to, resembling, or abounding in ice; cold; frosty.
